capabilities.description: Validates API keys and vault tokens against the secret store and rejects expired credentials. Use when the user asks to check a key. Do not use for session cookies or browser login state.
Manages browser session cookies for login flows and expiry rotation. Use when the user asks about cookies. Do not use for API keys or vault tokens.
Validates a JSON document against a JSON Schema draft and reports the first failing pointer. Use when checking schema compliance. Do not use for YAML frontmatter or Markdown prose.

Validates a capability record against a JSON Schema draft and reports the first failing pointer. Use when checking schema compliance of records. Do not use for YAML frontmatter or Markdown prose. Unlike json-schema-validate this is scoped to CapabilityRecord documents.
Parses YAML frontmatter from SKILL.md and rule files into a mapping. Use when the user asks to read frontmatter. Do not use for JSON Schema validation.
Drafts a git commit message from the staged diff and runs git commit. Use when the user asks to commit. Do not use for pushing remotes or force-updating branches.
Pushes the current branch to a named remote with explicit refspec. Use when the user asks to push. Do not use for drafting commit messages. Unlike git-commit this never writes a commit object.
Runs pytest on a selected path and returns the failing node ids. Use when the user asks to run tests. Do not use for lint or type-check.
Runs ruff check on Python files and returns rule codes. Use when the user asks to lint Python. Do not use for pytest execution.
Exposes local filesystem read and write through an MCP server. Use when a tool needs file bytes. Do not use for outbound HTTP or network fetch.
Fetches HTTP URLs through an MCP server and returns status plus body. Use when a tool needs a network GET. Do not use for local filesystem reads. Unlike mcp-filesystem this never opens a path.
Runs grok inspect --json against a rules file and prints load_mode. Use when measuring always-on versus lazy injection. Do not use for capability description lint.
Crawls the six capability roots into one index keyed by capability_id. Use when rebuilding the catalog census. Do not use for scoring description quality.
Redacts API keys from tool payloads before they reach the model. Use when a tool is about to run. Do not use for injecting extra context.

Writes Markdown documentation pages from a measured inventory.
Drafts changelog entries from merged pull requests.
Runs a shell command in the workspace and returns stdout. Use when the user asks to execute a command. Do not use for file edits; that is mcp.tool.edit.
Applies a surgical file edit at a given path. Use when the user asks to change a file. Do not use for shell commands; that is mcp.tool.shell.
Ranks corpus chunks by embedding cosine against a query. Use when the user wants semantic retrieval. Do not use for literal ripgrep. Unlike grep-search this recovers paraphrases.
Runs ripgrep over the worktree and returns matching file:line hits. Use when the user wants a literal string. Do not use for embedding cosine retrieval.
Runs ripgrep over the worktree and returns matching file:line hits. Use when the user wants a literal string in file contents.
Counts injected tokens with a real tokenizer, not an estimate.
Creates calendar events with timezone, attendees, and recurrence.
Generates raster images from a text prompt using a local diffusion checkpoint.
Applies Kubernetes manifests to a named cluster after a dry-run. Use when shipping a workload. Do not use for local pytest.
Keeps the web client signed in across requests and refreshes that state before it lapses; steer clear of it for credential checks.

Extract the metadata header at the top of a Markdown page as a dictionary.
Write a changeset description from the queued changes, then record a new revision in version control.
Execute the unit suite under a chosen directory and report which cases broke.
Execute static analysis over py sources and report the violated style identifiers.
Serves on-disk directory reads and writes over the model context protocol.
Retrieve a web address over the model context protocol and hand back the response code and payload.
Walk every skill, plugin, and hook directory and assemble a single lookup table of what is installed.
Scrub credentials out of an invocation's arguments prior to sending them to the LLM.
Roll out container orchestration specs onto the target environment once a rehearsal pass succeeds.
Order document passages by vector similarity to the question, finding meaning rather than exact words.
